title: Root-reclamation scheduler holds the state lock for seconds while planning (engram_named_root_reclamation.rs:388)
outcome: The test-run index tick's root-reclamation scheduling no longer holds the global state mutex for more than a short, bounded time under real multi-lane load, so mailbox, MCP-config and outstanding-work callers stop queueing behind it.
acceptance: AppState::schedule_engram_root_reclamation does its planning (engram_root_reclamation_plan_locked, engram_named_root_disposition_due_locked) without holding the state mutex for work proportional to the full state, or otherwise bounds that hold, with the observable decisions (flight single-flight, next_due, returned reason strings) unchanged.

A regression test proves that the hold is bounded, e.g. a scaled state where the scheduling hold stays under a stated bound while the plan contents equal the current implementation's, and the test fails against the current code.
Focused Rust tests for named-root reclamation and capacity pass on the exact input.
